title: High-cardinality ephemeral event fastpath and schema stitcher
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Problem: A subset of console usage events are high-cardinality, short-lived telemetry (eg. ephemeral preview tokens, per-request debug traces, transient session pings) that dominate write amplification and schema churn in the main ingestion path. These events cause frequent soft-failures in the schema validator, inflate storage costs, and increase tail latency for critical billing/metric events.

Goal: Implement a specialized fastpath that routes clearly-identified ephemeral/high-cardinality events through a lightweight ingest path that applies a staged validation approach (fast acceptance -> stitch metadata -> delayed strict validation), reducing tail latency and lowering rejection noise for the main pipeline. In parallel, introduce a "schema stitcher" service to materialize per-tenant effective schemas by composing canonical base schemas with tenant-specific extensions and runtime heuristics, instead of forcing all producers to fully conform to a single global contract.

Proposed design summary:
1) Classification layer (Ingress): augment the existing edge gateway with deterministic, low-cost classifiers (attribute-based rules + small bloom filter for known ephemeral ids) to tag events as EPHEMERAL_FASTPATH candidate. Rule set is pluggable and configurable via console.
2) Fastpath ingest service: lightweight write path that accepts candidate events with minimal synchronous validation (field presence + size quotas + coarse typing). Fastpath accepts events into a separate ephemeral store (tiered TTL) and emits a canonicalized lightweight envelope to the main pipeline for metrics/billing consumers.
3) Schema stitcher: service that composes an effective schema for a tenant at evaluation time by merging: canonical base schema, onboarding-time mapping rules, and sampled producer extensions. Stitcher exposes an API for the validator and for the offline reconciler. Stitcher computes schema diffs and suggested coercion rules (e.g., coerce string->int if >95% values parse).
4) Delayed strict validation: background reconciler consumes samples from fastpath store, runs full validation against the stitched schema, writes remediation suggestions to the console (alerts + suggested field mappings) and optionally backfills corrected events into the main pipeline.
5) Backpressure/fallbacks: if main pipeline is under pressure, fastpath keeps operating independently and will mark events with ingestion metadata so consumers can opt-in for approximate results.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Pros: reduces tail latency for critical events; lowers noise in validator alerts; provides a practical on-ramp for producers with high cardinality; isolates cost.
- Cons: increases system complexity (new service, store, and reconciliation loop); potential for data divergence if backfill fails; operator burden for rule tuning.

Operational objectives and SLOs:
- Fastpath write latency p95 < 70ms under normal load.
- No increase in billing-event main-path p99 by more than 0.5s during rollout.
- Validation alert volume for canonical pipelines down by 30% after 2 weeks.
- Backfill success rate >= 95% for reconciled events.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Edge classifier can tag ephemeral candidates with <1ms median added latency and <2% false positive rate on a sampled production trace.
2) Fastpath accepts and persists a 5k RPS synthetic ephemeral workload for 48 hours without increased error rates.
3) Schema stitcher can produce a merged schema for a tenant (<=500 fields) in <150ms and expose a diff with suggested coercions.
4) End-to-end test demonstrating delayed strict validation identifies a schema mismatch and backfills corrected event into the main stream.
5) Monitored dashboards and alerts created: fastpath-latency, fastpath-drop-rate, stitcher-latency, reconciliation-failures.
6) Feature flag gate + canary plan documented and executed (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
